extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, institutional research administrators, and grant applicants
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy updates, resources, and guidance relevant to grant applicants and administrators. It highlights topics such as model selection, new application formats, data management plans, replication/reproducibility, and peer review changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of research models
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions; NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential. Choose models that are scientifically sound and aligned to the study aims rather than selecting models for novelty alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand PF5 (Collaborative International Research Projects) application format and award structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the video to learn format specifics and procedures (including potential splitting into linked awards) so proposals conform to PF5 expectations and administrative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare DMS Plans using the 2026 pilot format and include the required elements as specified by NIH. The update represents a simplified set of required elements — follow the new template rather than older formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout research and applications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances a commitment to replication and reproducibility and has launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees should consider including plans, methods, or justifications that promote reproducibility and replication. Emphasize experimental design, transparency, and practices that enhance reliability of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that an application scored as 'competitive but not discussed' indicates it was in the middle third after initial cuts and therefore was not discussed in detail; this reflects emergency modifications implemented after the lapse in appropriations and affects post-review expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of centralized peer review changes
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review was centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of consolidation of peer review processes and that centralization may affect review handling, study section assignment, and timing. Stay informed about CSR procedures and any related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NIH resources (Data Book, news, and announcements) to stay informed
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH posts updates such as Fiscal Year data in the NIH Data Book, meeting schedules for National Advisory Councils or Boards, and other announcements relevant to grant applicants and administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscribe to NIH Extramural Nexus emails and consult the NIH Data Book and news posts to keep current on policy changes, calendar items, and resources that may affect applications and awards.
